body: Somawathiya Temple is a serene and spiritually significant Buddhist shrine in Sri Lanka, renowned for enshrining a sacred relic of the Buddha’s tooth. Surrounded by lush greenery and the flowing Mahaweli River, it offers a tranquil atmosphere for worship and reflection. The temple holds great cultural and religious importance, drawing pilgrims and visitors seeking blessings and peace. Its historical value, combined with the natural beauty of the surroundings, makes Somawathiya not just a place of worship but also a destination of heritage and serenity.
title: Somawathiya Temple offers a serene blend of spirituality, history, and natural beauty—perfect for peaceful reflection.

body: Somawathiya Chaitya is a Buddhist Stupa situated approximately 45 minutes away from the ancient city of Polonnaruwa of Ceylon. The said holy ground, Chaitya premises, is called the Somawathiya Rajamaha Viharaya. Surrounded by the Somawathiya forest reserve, the stupa is located on the left bank of the Mahaweli River of Ceylon. This wonderful stupa is believed to have been built in the reign of King Kavantissa – King Dutugemunu’s father - who ruled the Magama region of Ceylon. It’s said to enshrine the right canine tooth relic of the Lord Buddha, one of the four tooth relics, which are considered the most sacred relics by Buddhists of Ceylon and around the world. Somawathiya is therefore much older than Ruwanveliseya of Anuradhapura, Mirisaveti Vihara or Jetawanaramaya of Anuradhapura in Ceylon. Amazing nature, you will come across Elephants during the journey to the said holy grounds, in my experience.
title: Holy site Somawathiya Rajamaha Viharaya of Ceylon

body: Somawathi Chethiya was built in the 2nd century BC and this stupa is said to enshrine the Right Tooth Relic of Buddha. The Somawathi Chethiya is located about 20 km north east of Polonnaruwa, by the bank of the Mahaveli River within the Sanctuary. The 'Flood Plains' of Mahaveli river have been inhibited by a large number of wild animals ranging from elephants, wild buffalo, deer and other animals. This Chethiya had been abandoned for more than fifteen years due to the threat of war. According to the ancient chronicles of Sri Lanka the very first Arahat of this country Ven. Aritta, visited the abode of Gods and brought back to Sri Lanka the Sacred Right Tooth Relic of the Buddha. This Sacred Relic was handed to king Giri Abha and his consort Queen Somawathie who was King Kavantissa's sister. Queen Somawathie dedicated and construct a Stupa in adoration of the Buddha at Somapura.It is believed that one of the only two tooth relics of Buddha existing in the world is at the Somawathiya and the other one is at the Dalada Maligawa, Kandy. It is the very reason that thousands of pilgrims pay their homage to this chethiya. Archaeologists have found four moonstones and flower pedestals excavating around the chethiya. In addition to these many buildings have been unearthed including a wall surrounding the stupa. Out of the nine stone inscriptions found around this site, the most well-known are the four inscriptions found on the Eric Swan Rock. This rock can be seen a few metres away from the road, about 100 metres before the main entrance to the temple. This rock was named Eric Swan Rock, after a photographer named Eric Swan, who was killed by a wild elephant near this rock.
title: Somawathiya Chaitya

body: Somawathi Stupa is located in the middle of the jungle, in Polonnaruwa district. From Polonnaruwa, you have to travel to Sungavila and then take a lengthy road which leads to the temple through the Jungle. Early days this was a dusty gravel road, but recent road construction enabled devotees to reach this grate stupa without much hassle. Its recommended to go Somawathiya in dry season, because there is a probability that the area get flooded during the raining time.Somawathi stupa has written historical evidence that it was constructed in 2nd century BC. This dageba was named for the princes Somawathi, the sister of king Kawanthissa.. She got married to prince Abhaya, a nephew of of king Shiva of Kelaniya. He was the ruler of the Somapura Kingdom, which was located by the Mahaveli river.They constructed a new temple in their kingdom and searching for a "dathu" to deposit in the stupa. They received the right side tooth relic of load Buddha from reverent arahath Mahinda thero. According to the historical facts, this dageba was constructed with depositing them.
title: Must visit stupa as a Buddhist or history lover

Miraculous Place
body: One of the best "lost temples" of the world where miracles are said to happen in front of your eyes. This is another place where relics of Lord Gauthama Buddha is said to house within the temple. There're pictures of an entire procession coming out of the perfectly enclosed temple which could only be photographed. Also there're pictures of a small white elephant running into the temple & disappearing. During the civil war with the LTTE, the monks of the temple say that the wild elephants would come out of the jungle in the evening & stand guard of the temple & the holy relic of Buddha so that the terrorists would attack. Many have even photographs of such situations. Several months of the year, the temple becomes inaccessible due to floods, where the monks use a boat to go to the temple & worship it. Best visit the temple before 8am since many hundreds of people come everyday to worship.
